headline: 5,418 passengers stranded as 51 flights from Dhaka to Saudi Arabia cancelled
summary: Cancellations affect routes to Riyadh, Dammam, and Jeddah following Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports.
details: Over 5,400 passengers are stranded in Bangladesh after airlines cancelled 51 flights to Riyadh, Dammam, and Jeddah from Saturday through October 15.
The cancellations were triggered by Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, including a missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 13 people, including two Bangladeshis.
Direct services from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Riyadh Air, and Saudia were affected, alongside 39 transit flights via carriers like IndiGo, Emirates, and Qatar Airways.
A second attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani expatriate and injured 11 others. The Houthis used ballistic and cruise missiles and drones to target the airports.
Houthi military spokesperson Brig Gen Yahya Saree warned that all Saudi airports, except those in Makkah and Medina, could be targets of future attacks.
caption:
Over 5,400 passengers are stranded in Dhaka as 51 flights to Saudi Arabia are cancelled.

Over 5,400 passengers are stranded in Bangladesh after airlines cancelled 51 flights to Riyadh, Dammam, and Jeddah from Saturday through October 15.

The cancellations were triggered by Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, including a missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 13 people, including two Bangladeshis.

Direct services from Biman Bangladesh Airlines, US-Bangla Airlines, Riyadh Air, and Saudia were affected, alongside 39 transit flights via carriers like IndiGo, Emirates, and Qatar Airways.

A second attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani expatriate and injured 11 others. The Houthis used ballistic and cruise missiles and drones to target the airports.

Houthi military spokesperson Brig Gen Yahya Saree warned that all Saudi airports, except those in Makkah and Medina, could be targets of future attacks.

headline: 5 units of Fire Service fire breaks out at a shop in Chawkbazar
summary: The blaze occurred on the sixth floor of Monjur Khan Plaza in the Choto Katara area of the capital.
details: A fire broke out at a shop on the sixth floor of Monjur Khan Plaza in the Choto Katara area of Chawkbazar, Dhaka.
According to the Fire Service, the blaze started at 5:02 PM on Monday.
Fire Service units were notified of the incident at 5:04 PM and immediately dispatched to the scene.
Five units of the Fire Service are currently working to bring the fire under control.
No immediate information regarding casualties or the extent of property damage has been reported.
